newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf Coast draws more North Sea barrels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf Coast draws more North Sea barrels.

text.p: The U.S. Gulf Coast drew more offers for transatlantic crude on Tuesday in response to improved economics, traders said.
A European major continued to show Brent crude into the Gulf for around May 10-15 arrival, asking a discount of some 90 cents off West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
The company sold at least two cargoes on Monday into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP) for delivery up Capline to Canadian refiners, traders said.
The cargoes were sold around WTI minus $1.00-10 a barrel.
A Wall Street trader was talking Brent for end-May delivery, asking 60-70 cents under WTI/Cushing.
The spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.85-90 a barrel Tuesday afternoon, encouraging sellers to move transatlantic cargoes.

Meanwhile, light West African cargoes remained plentiful. Forcados was offered around dated Brent plus $1.30-35 and Qua Iboe at dated Brent plus $1.70-75 delivered for the second half of May, traders said.
Heavy sweet grades from West Africa such as Cabinda were scarce amid Asian buying, traders said.
From Latin America, a strengthening of the sour crude market gave short-haul sour producers a respite, however temporary.

Sour crudes were up around 20 cents from last week amid the continued closure of two key Mexican ports due to severe weather and the temporary shutdown of the Mars platform in the Gulf of Mexico, traders said.
The Mexican ports of Dos Bocas and Pajaritos were not expected to reopen until Wednesday, local officials said. Two crude tankers were stuck waiting to load at Dos Bocas.

The Shell-operated Mars platform in the deepwater Gulf Of Mexico went down last Friday afternoon because of an electrical failure. The platform was gradually coming back up to normal levels, a Shell spokesperson said.
Shell and partner British Petroleum pump around 86,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Mar crude, a medium sour grade with an API gravity of 31 degrees.
Venezuelan Mesa crude was pegged around $3.80 a barrel under WTI, up some 20 cents from late last week.
